independentIdentityRefreshAcceptance.scope: All six complete old/current Nevada tracks, global metadata, unrelated receipt fields, exact prior refresh and original identity preservation; no source-byte changes or runtime authority.

Removed special-route prosecutor stipulations are not missing required components under the retained correction contract. Proposed orders/declarations are identified as prepared supporting documents, not official or newly mandated forms.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.finding: All 76 canonical and all 76 boundary known values were independently read from their own component pages. No expected known value is missing or invisible, including long boundary identity and contact values.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: All 84 current required facts have exact participant-guide labels and supply instructions. Caption court, actual case/charge/decriminalizing law/pardon proof and narrative facts remain participant-supplied. The initial internal-identity-string guide probe was invalid; the preserved corrected document-heading and exact-label audit finds zero omitted disclosures.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.finding: The six route sets are explicit; no checkbox election is silently made. Automatic-first pardon, traffic/decriminalization boundaries, actual record proof, and ordinary route conditions remain stated. Unknown status, legal classification, conviction date, charge scope, court and proof are not invented.

REPEATING_ROWS.finding: These composed pleadings contain no repeating-row election control. Record/case/agency lists and narratives remain actual-data requirements; no partial populated repeating row is delivered.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.finding: All 84 protected court, prosecutor, clerk, agency, participant-execution, date and notary fields remain refusals, with no reported write intersection. Current changed actual pages were read for those blanks; the unchanged ordinary page identities preserve the earlier independent findings.

ARTIFACTS.finding: The canonical 122,964-byte and boundary 125,173-byte whole PDFs each contain 44 pages. Their Git, inventory and current central document hashes agree at the immutable review base; both exact PDF anchors are declared below. No optional or diagnostic extra document is counted.

PAGE_ORDER.finding: Both 44-entry page manifests cover sequential pages 1–44 and the same exact 28-component order, with each component’s source pages contiguous. The changed guide continuations and boundary page breaks are legible and correctly sequenced.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.finding: All 20 changed actual central PNGs were independently viewed at original resolution in this session: zero clipping/overlap. The other 68 current ordinary pages inherit only CODEX-CS2-FIX18’s original independent page findings via successful immutable CI pixel identity. This is 20 newly viewed + 68 explicitly reused, not a claim of 88 new views or reuse of old special pages.

FILING_DESTINATION.finding: Changed decriminalization requests go directly to the convicting court; pardon first checks automatic sealing and, where a petition is needed, submits actual pardon proof to a convicting court. Neither route requires prosecutor preapproval. The four ordinary route destinations and venue distinctions are unchanged from the independently reviewed sources/output.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: Both changed guides explicitly state their special petition/request submission is free under the retained 179.271(2)/179.273(5) contract, without an indigency/fee-waiver prerequisite. Separate record/service charges and the existing 179.245(9) protection remain distinct. Ordinary-route fee content is unchanged. The VF12 contradictory pardon fee and later decriminalization fee defect are absent.

SERVICE.finding: Decriminalization uses court-sent written notice and ten judicial days from prosecutor receipt, not filing date or the ordinary thirty-day period; objection leads to a hearing/legal-help stop. Pardon excludes prosecutor/criminal-agency review and stipulation. Post-order repository/custodian distribution remains stated. Ordinary-route instructions are unchanged.

SELF_HELP_STOP.finding: Changed guides retain unknown law/status and record scope, traffic exclusion, conditional/ambiguous or non-Nevada pardon, absent proof or mismatched charges, contested/denied court action and collateral-consequence stops. Ordinary legal classification, timing, pending charge, multicourt and jurisdiction stops remain unchanged. The packet does not decide immigration/firearm consequences or supply unknown proof.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.finding: All 70 ledger blanks are disclosed, but there are 24 further blanks the ledger never contains — one caption court line on every captioned page — and what the packet prints beneath them tells the participant to write a prosecutor's office where the court belongs.

theDefect.blindSpotConfirmedNotAssumed: this family is one of the 40 in data/rcap-grade-a/packet-completeness/UNCLASSIFIED_BLANKS_BLIND_SPOT.json. I tested it rather than assuming it: I searched all 410 field-map rows for a caption-court blank. Ninety-eight rows mention a court; every one is a case-number row, a court-owned decision, signing or date line, or a declaration field. None is the caption's court blank. So unclassifiedBlanks reports 0 because it structurally cannot see these, not because they are absent.

countedFromTheBytes.spread: one on every captioned page across all six routes

theDefect.andThisIsWhyItIsAFailHere: on the other composed families in this roster the caption blank is unregistered but self-labelling: the line beneath prints the exact court to write. Here the line beneath prints '(The district attorney's or city attorney's office first, then the clerk of the appropriate court - see the filing instructions in this packet)'. That is the route's DESTINATION, not its VENUE, and it is printed directly under a blank whose own printed text reads 'IN THE ______ COURT'. A participant following it literally captions a court petition with a prosecutor's office.
theDefect.whatShouldBeThere: the registry holds the venue for every one of the six routes and the packet prints it correctly elsewhere. For nv_seal_conviction the registry venue is 'The court in which the person was convicted, being a district, justice or municipal court. NRS 179.245(1).' The packet's own FILING_DESTINATION cell prints exactly that under 'Venue as recorded'. The caption parenthetical reaches for the destination string instead of the venue string.
theDefect.thePacketKnowsTheDistinctionElsewhere: item C9 on the nv_seal_multi route asks 'For any justice court case, which township? (Asked because justice court petitions must be captioned to the specific township.)' — the packet knows the caption must name a court and a township, asks the participant for the township, and then never gives them a place or an instruction to write either.
theDefect.whyThisIsNotCosmetic: a Nevada sealing petition is filed with the clerk of the convicting court after the prosecutor stipulates. A caption naming the district attorney's office is not a caption that court will accept, and the participant has been told by the packet itself to write it.

evidence.residualObservation: the repair is small and bounded: register a caption-court blank per captioned page, and change the parenthetical to the venue string the family already holds. No fixture text outside the caption line need move.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.finding: On five of the six routes the fee cell is correct. On the pardon route the packet prints the chapter-wide default — county-dependent, apply for a waiver — for a petition whose own statutory title, quoted by this same packet six lines earlier, says it carries no fee.

fiveRoutesCorrect.statedFee: County-dependent, plus the repository criminal history and fingerprinting costs and certified copies. Every fee is waived for a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude under NRS 179.245(9).
fiveRoutesCorrect.whyCorrect: the registry's own fees field for each of those tracks says exactly that, and src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/NV-nevada.json packetGenerator.feeRules is an empty array, so 'county-dependent' is the repository's own answer and not a delegation of an answered fact
fiveRoutesCorrect.andTheCrossCuttingWaiverIsSurfaced: NRS 179.245(9) zeroes every fee in the process for a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude, including fingerprints, criminal history and certified copies; the registry requires it to be surfaced wherever a fee is mentioned, and the packet surfaces it in all six cells

theFailingRoute.whatThePacketPrintsUnderTheCostHeading: WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHETHER A WAIVER EXISTS — Fee as recorded: County-dependent, plus the repository criminal history and fingerprinting costs and certified copies ... Fee waiver as recorded: NRS 179.245(9) for a victim of sex trafficking or involuntary servitude; county fee-waiver applications otherwise.
theFailingRoute.whatTheSamePagePrintsSixLinesEarlier: NRS 179.273 is titled "Sealing of records after unconditional pardon: Automatic sealing; petition; no fee" ... Because sealing is automatic in the first instance, the petition route exists only where the automatic sealing has not happened, and it carries no fee.
theFailingRoute.soThePacketContradictsItselfOnOnePage: under the heading a participant reads to learn what filing costs, the packet gives a county-dependent fee and a waiver to apply for; six lines above, it states the petition carries no fee. Both statements are in the delivered bytes of the same component.
theFailingRoute.whatTheBoundRecordHolds: legal-design-track-registry.json, track nv_seal_pardon: mechanism records the section's official title including 'no fee'; waitingPeriods.duration records 'none. The section provides automatic sealing, with a no-fee petition available where it has not occurred'; and an open question carries sourceStatement 'NRS 179.273 Sealing of records after unconditional pardon: Automatic sealing; petition; no fee'.
theFailingRoute.theA3Failure: the fee was read at chapter level rather than per route. NRS 179.245(9)'s waiver and the county-dependent default belong to the ordinary sealing petition; NRS 179.273's petition is a different instrument with its own recorded fee answer, and the record states that answer.
theFailingRoute.theA4Failure: the packet tells the participant, under the cost heading, that the cost is county-dependent and that they may need a waiver, when a record it binds — and text it prints itself — states the petition carries no fee.
theFailingRoute.consequenceForAParticipant: a person with an unconditional pardon may prepare a county fee-waiver application, or budget for a filing fee, on a petition the statute's own title says is free.
theFailingRoute.whatTheRepairIsNot: the registry records that the full text of NRS 179.273 is an open question, so the repair is not to assert the section's mechanics. It is to make the pardon route's cost cell state the no-fee answer the record holds, and to keep the NRS 179.245(9) waiver where it belongs — on the fees that do exist, such as the Central Repository criminal history and fingerprinting.

evidence.anAdjacentObservationNotScoredAsASeparat: the same route's own record states that NRS 179.273 provides AUTOMATIC sealing, with the petition available only where the automatic sealing has not occurred. The packet does carry this — the pardon route's item C10 asks 'Have you checked whether the record still shows on your Nevada criminal history? (Asked first, because sealing under this section is automatic and a petition should only be prepared where verification shows it did not happen.)' — so the automatic-first ordering is present and is not a second defect.
